rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: COSHH requires employers to protect workers against risks from hazardous construction dusts.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: Construction dust includes silica dust, non-silica dust and wood dust.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: Cutting, drilling and grinding materials such as concrete and mortar can release respirable crystalline silica.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: Regularly breathing construction dust can cause lung cancer, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and silicosis.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: HSE describes an Assess, Control and Review model for managing construction-dust risks.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: Respirable crystalline silica can be too fine to see under normal lighting but can still penetrate deeply into the lungs.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: Task guidance for construction silica uses controls such as dust extraction, water suppression and suitable respiratory protection.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: Construction-silica controls must be followed in full or replaced by measures that are equally effective.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: Construction-dust risk depends on material composition, task, duration, control equipment, ventilation, RPE fit, housekeeping and measured exposure.

rows.source: HSE construction-dust and respirable crystalline silica guidance
rows.verified: General assessment and control of silica, non-silica and wood dust generated by construction work guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: All welding fume can cause lung cancer and employers must control exposure even where the amount of welding is small.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: The control hierarchy is to avoid or reduce welding-fume exposure, use local exhaust ventilation and then use suitable respiratory protective equipment where needed.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: Indoor welding should use local exhaust ventilation to remove fume at source when welding cannot be avoided.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: Suitable respiratory protective equipment is required where local exhaust ventilation alone does not adequately control exposure or cannot reasonably be used.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: Outdoor welding generally requires suitable respiratory protection because local exhaust ventilation will not work effectively outdoors.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: Welding-fume local exhaust ventilation must be thoroughly examined and tested by a competent person at least every 14 months, with records kept for at least five years.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: Health surveillance should be provided where the risk assessment identifies a need, including respiratory surveillance for relevant asthmagen exposure.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: Welding workers need training on health risks, likely exposure, safe technique, pre-use checks, control use, respiratory protection and emergency action.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: Welding-fume risk depends on process, material and coating, duration, position, enclosure, LEV capture, ventilation, RPE selection and worker technique.

rows.source: HSE welding-fume risk-control guidance
rows.verified: General avoidance, extraction, respiratory protection, maintenance, surveillance and training for welding fume guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.
